title: Rock Stars Help a Music School for Kids Celebrate 25 Years
summary:
Some of rock music's biggest bands came together on Saturday to celebrate a music school for kids. The Silverlake Conservatory of Music held a 25th anniversary benefit concert at the Hollywood Palladium in Los Angeles. A benefit concert raises money for a cause.

The school was founded in 2001 by Flea, the bass player of Red Hot Chili Peppers, along with Keith "Tree" Barry and their friend Peter Weiss. It helps fill gaps in music education in Los Angeles public schools and gives music lessons to 1,000 students each week. Its scholarship program helps more than 200 students whose families could not otherwise afford lessons. Those students get free lessons, instruments, supplies and classes.

The night began with the students themselves. A student group called the SCM All Stars played songs including "Love Rollercoaster," and a student brass band called the Hollywood Highsteppers performed too. Because it was Flea's birthday weekend, the brass band played "When the Saints Go Marching In" as he was given a birthday cake on stage.

Anahit, a member of the All Stars, has been taking lessons at the school since she was 6. "Music has always been an emotional outlet," she said.

Rapper Vince Staples performed with a band that includes two former students of the school. Dave Grohl then played songs including "My Hero," and his band, Foo Fighters, surprised the crowd by joining him on stage. His daughter Violet sang with them too.

Red Hot Chili Peppers closed the show with an 11-song set, including rare songs they had not played live in many years. The night ended with the crowd singing along to "Give It Away."

"It brings such a good community," Anahit said of the school.
why_it_matters: Music lessons can be expensive, and programs like this help kids who could not otherwise afford them learn to play. The concert shows how famous musicians can use their fame to support young learners.
